annotation.title_clean: Proposal for a Regulation of the European Parliament and of the Council amending Regulations (EU) 2017/745 and (EU) 2017/746 as regards simplifying and reducing the burden of the rules on medical devices and in vitro diagnostic medical devices, and amending Regulation (EU) 2022/123 and Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 as regards the list of Union harmonisation legislation referred to in its Annex I
annotation.title_en: Proposal for a Regulation amending the Medical Devices Regulation and IVD Regulation (simplification and burden reduction), Regulation (EU) 2022/123 and the AI Act Annex I
named_instruments_referenced: Charter of Fundamental Rights of the EU
annotation.summary_en: This is the European Commission's December 2025 proposal to simplify the EU Medical Devices (MDR) and In Vitro Diagnostics (IVDR) Regulations. It changes conformity assessment, notified-body oversight, clinical evidence and reporting rules. It adds regulatory sandboxes and cybersecurity incident reporting. It also moves the MDR and IVDR to Section B of AI Act Annex I, so only some AI Act provisions apply to AI-enabled devices.
key_provisions_or_claims: Moves the MDR and IVDR from Section A to Section B of AI Act Annex I; the Commission must consider AI Act Chapter III Section 2 requirements when adopting rules for AI-enabled devices
Removes the 5-year maximum validity of certificates in favour of risk-proportionate periodic reviews; lowers notified-body involvement for lower and medium-risk devices
Introduces priority and rolling reviews for breakthrough and orphan devices, and lets Member States and the Commission set up regulatory sandboxes
Requires reporting of cybersecurity vulnerabilities and incidents to CSIRTs and ENISA through Eudamed
Uses joint assessment teams to strengthen oversight of notified bodies, and expands the roles of expert panels and EMA support
